To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Arabidopsis RNA helicase ISE1 and the DEVH helicase Ise2 regulate PD development and function, plastid development, and the expression of several cell wall synthesis and remodeling genes.

RNA helicases ISE1 and ISE2 are required to maintain normal plastid development and PD structure/function, and that both organelles are involved in the same signaling pathway that regulates PD transport.

the mitochondrial DEAD-box RNA Helicase ISE1 and the Chloroplast RNA Helicase (DEVH) ISE2 are both required for normal embryonic development and that ISE1 and ISE2 are required for the normal formation of the PD and for normal plastid development.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the regulation of intercellular transport in plants, which has important implications for the development of plant cell–cell communication networks and for understanding how plants sense and respond to biotic and abiotic stressors.
how plants regulate cell-to-cell communication and how these processes are affected by environmental conditions.
understanding how plant cells communicate via PD, which is a critical component of plant development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the two mutants identified in this screen, ise1 and ise 2, have altered plastid development and function, altered PD development/function and altered expression of a subset of genes with a role in both of these processes.
the ISE2 protein is a chloroplast localized DEVH-type RNA-helicase that is required for proper plastid development and that it functions in a novel organelle–plasmodesma–nucleus signaling pathway.
the RNA helicases ISE1 and ISE2 regulate the expression of genes encoding plastid-localized proteins, and this regulation is critical for plastid development and function.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
organelle–PD signaling is critical for plant development, and that this signaling is mediated by RNA helicases, which are likely to be part of the signaling pathway.

the ISE1 and ISE2 RNA helicases, which localize to the mitochondria and the chloroplasts, respectively, have a role in regulating the intercellular transport capacity of PD and in regulating chloroplast development.
organelle–plasmodesmata–nucleus communication is a new signaling pathway for regulating plant cell development and communication.
The main takeaway from our work is that
organelle–organelle–nuclear cross-talk is essential for normal plant growth and development.
RNA helicases are critical regulators of organelle–plasmodesma communication.

the cell is not a simple compartmentalized entity, but rather a complex system in which organelles and cytoplasmic components are tightly integrated to enable the cell to function as an integrated unit.
